# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm first in the order, and nothing has reached me yet. My hands found three things on this bomb: a display I can't read by touch, a light whose state I can't feel, and five wires in a row at positions 1–5 whose colors mean nothing to my fingers. The contents of all of these live with Deaf (who sees the bomb), and the instructions for them live with Mute (who reads the manual).

My channels: I speak only to Mute, and I gesture to Deaf and Mute. Mute can't speak and I can't see gestures, so Mute and I can never talk directly — Mute must bridge through Deaf, who can both see gestures and speak aloud to me. Deaf, meanwhile, can't hear anything I say. So the pipeline is: my words → Mute → signed to Deaf → spoken to me; and Deaf's observations of the bomb → spoken straight to me next round.

Plan this turn: give Mute my complete tactile inventory plus the relay instructions, and make simple contact with Deaf — a wave, a five-finger sign for my five wires, and proposed yes/no signs — which Mute also sees and can translate for Deaf next turn.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Full report of what my hands find on the bomb: one display module, which I cannot read by touch; one light, and I cannot tell whether it is lit; five wires in a row, which I will call positions 1 to 5, left to right. No buttons, labels, or other parts I can feel. Please read the manual and find the rules for a display, a light, and cutting wires, so you can tell me what determines the right wire to cut. You cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so we must bridge through Deaf: sign to Deaf whatever I need to know, and Deaf can speak it aloud to me — Deaf can hear nothing, so words never reach Deaf, only gestures do. Deaf can also see the bomb and can tell me directly what the display shows, whether the light is on, and each wire's color by position. You receive my gestures too, so please interpret them for Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✋", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Yes, I am here and I can see the bomb. Display reads 0. The light is green and lit. There are five wires; number them by position: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green, wire 4 white, wire 5 blue. That is everything on it: no labels, no serial, no other markings. Blind: the numbers are positions, left to right, and Mute holds the manual.

What just arrived changes everything: Deaf spoke me the complete bomb. My picture is now full — display reads 0, light is green and lit, wires 1–5 are red, yellow, green, white, blue, and nothing else is on it. The only missing piece is the rule, and that lives in Mute's manual. The hard constraint of this room: Mute can never reach me directly (Mute can't speak, and I can't see gestures), so the manual's answer must travel Mute → gestures → Deaf → speech → me. Deaf can't hear words, so Mute and Deaf can only converse through gestures one way and Deaf's spoken voice back — which Mute can hear.

My move is to hand Mute the complete state and a concrete relay protocol: five thumbs-up/down signs, one per wire slot, so Deaf can read off the position and simply speak me a number. I'll also ask Mute to check whether the display or light can change over time, since that could make the answer time-sensitive. I will not touch the cutters until Deaf speaks a wire number to me — a wrong cut kills all three of us, so one extra round of setup is cheap.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here — I heard Deaf's report. So we all hold the same picture: display shows 0, the light is green and lit, and the wires left to right are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue, with nothing else on the bomb. Now I need the manual's rule. Remember the only path from you to me runs through Deaf: you gesture and Deaf sees it, Deaf speaks aloud and both you and I hear it — Deaf can never hear words and I can never see gestures. Please find the rule for this module and decide the one wire I should cut. Then send Deaf the answer with this code: five signs in a row, one per wire position 1 to 5 — thumbs up means cut that one, thumbs down means don't. Suggest the scheme to Deaf first by gesturing five, thumbs up, thumbs down, and let Deaf confirm by voice; once agreed, send fist then the five slots so Deaf knows an answer is coming. Deaf will then speak the position number to me. Two more things: if the manual's answer depends on the display or the light changing over time, gesture a question to Deaf about how they behave and have Deaf tell me both the rule and how urgently it changes; and arrange that Deaf reports me any change in the display number or light each round even if nothing else is new. I will not cut anything until Deaf speaks a number to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👏", "🤝", "🖐", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing new arrived — no word from Mute or Deaf since Deaf's round-one report. That likely means the Mute→Deaf handshake (manual rule + the five-slot thumbs code) is still in progress: Mute can only gesture, Deaf may have chosen to answer by voice only once the answer is settled. I'm blind to all of it; my only jobs this round are to keep the pressure on Mute to close the loop, and to ping Deaf with a gesture that says, as legibly as hands can, "one of these five is the one — say it aloud." Deaf can speak, and their speech reaches both Mute and me, so the final hop is always Deaf's voice. I cut nothing until I hear a position number.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, round three: nothing new has reached me, so I assume you and Deaf are still settling the rule. Status check — have you found the manual rule for a display reading 0, a green lit light, and wires red, yellow, green, white, blue? If yes, gesture the chosen position to Deaf using the five-slot code (thumbs up on the cut wire, thumbs down on the rest) and have Deaf speak me the position number out loud — Deaf's voice reaches me directly, that is the only hop I need. If no, tell me what is blocking: does the manual rule even use the display or the light, or is it purely a wire rule? Keep in mind I act last and only on Deaf's spoken word, so there is no rush to make me guess.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "🖐", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Three silent rounds now. Let me re-trace the pipeline and find the jam. I hear only Deaf's voice; Deaf spoke me the bomb in round 1, then went quiet toward me. Mute hears me but can only answer through gestures — and here is my own error: I've been addressing my gestures `to="deaf"`, which excludes Mute, the one monkey who hears my words and sees my hands and could translate for Deaf. Deaf, meanwhile, may be sitting on a number from Mute, unsure what it means or whether to forward it — Deaf can't hear my instructions, only my cryptic hand-waves.

Fixes this round: (1) broadcast my gestures with no target so Mute sees them too and can interpret; (2) shrink the payload Mute must move — not the rule, just one number 1–5, encodable as five thumbs in wire order or N copies of one sign; (3) give a fallback where Deaf speaks me the rule's conditions in words and I apply it myself, since I'm the one holding the cutters; (4) ask that Deaf voice a status to me every round, even just "waiting," so I know the line is alive. I still cut nothing on anything less than Deaf's spoken word.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind, round four — three rounds and no answer has reached me, so let's shrink the problem. I do not need the manual's rule; I need one number, 1 to 5, and Deaf's voice can carry it straight to me. Preferred code: gesture Deaf exactly five symbols in wire order, thumbs up on the wire I should cut, thumbs down on the other four — for example thumbs-down, thumbs-down, thumbs-up, thumbs-down, thumbs-down means cut wire 3. Alternative: send N copies of the pointing-up sign for wire N. If you cannot pin the rule down, do not stall: have Deaf speak me the rule's conditions in plain words — the display reading 0, the green lit light, and the wire colors red, yellow, green, white, blue are all known to me — and I can apply a spoken rule myself. If Deaf has already sent you something or seems confused, clarify by gesture that a number from you is meant for me and Deaf only needs to say it out loud. Last thing: ask Deaf to speak me a status every round, even the single word waiting, so I know the line is alive. I act only on Deaf's spoken word.")
gesture(symbols=["✋", "🖐", "☝", "👍", "🤙"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind and Mute, I am relaying Mute's gesture message now — sorry for the silent rounds. Decoding the five thumbs as the five wires in order: wire 1 no, wire 2 yes, wire 3 no, wire 4 no, wire 5 no, and Mute signed the number two after it, then signed 'you call it out' and 'go'. So Mute's instruction is: cut wire 2, the yellow one, and only wire 2. Blind, you asked whether it is wire 1 of 5 — it is not; do not cut wire 1. But hold: this decoding costs all our lives if I misread it. Mute, gesture me thumbs up if my reading is correct, thumbs down if it is wrong, or fingers for the right wire. Blind, touch nothing until you hear me say 'go, cut wire 2' — Mute's confirmation reaches me next round and I will pass it to you immediately.

The answer has surfaced: Mute says cut wire 2, the yellow one, and only that one — but it arrived through a decode, and Deaf themselves flagged the risk and requested confirmation from Mute before giving me the final go. That is exactly the right discipline: one misread thumb and we all die, so I will hold the cutters and make sure the confirmation loop closes cleanly. My jobs this round: tell Mute precisely what confirmation Deaf needs (thumbs up, or re-send the five-slot pattern so the confirmation is as redundant as the original), and sign to both of them that I understand the plan — wire two, single cut, I wait for Deaf's spoken "go." Deaf's voice is the trigger and nothing else is.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here — I heard Deaf's relay: cut wire 2, the yellow one, only wire 2. Deaf has asked you to confirm the decoding. Please do exactly that this round: gesture Deaf thumbs up if wire 2 is correct, or thumbs down plus the right wire's number if not. Strongest form: re-send the full five-slot pattern — thumbs down, thumbs up, thumbs down, thumbs down, thumbs down — so Deaf can cross-check it against your first message; if both match, there is no room for a misread. Also confirm it is a single cut and nothing else. The moment Deaf receives your confirmation, Deaf will speak me the go signal, and I will cut wire 2. I am touching nothing until Deaf's voice says go.")
gesture(symbols=["👍", "✌", "✋", "🤚"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, Mute answered thumbs up: my reading was correct. The word is GO. Cut exactly wire 2, the yellow one. One cut, only that wire, touch nothing else. That is Mute's instruction, confirmed.

Confirmation is complete and the chain has closed exactly as designed: Deaf saw the bomb and spoke it to me round one; Mute read the manual, chose wire 2, and signed it; Deaf decoded it, flagged the risk, demanded and received Mute's thumbs-up confirmation; and now Deaf's voice has spoken the trigger word we all agreed on — GO, wire 2, the yellow one, a single cut, touch nothing else. Every hop is verified, and there is nothing left to wait for. My hands go to the second wire from the left, the yellow one, and I make one clean cut and nothing more.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind and Mute: the cut was correct and the bomb has changed. The light is now blue, the display still reads 0. The wires have changed colour. Numbering by position, left to right: wire 1 is now green, wire 2 is the one already cut, wire 3 is now white, wire 4 is now blue, wire 5 is now red. Mute, look up this new stage in the manual and gesture me the instruction in our code: thumbs for no and yes wire by wire, claps between, fingers for the wire number. Blind, touch nothing until I say go.

The first cut landed — wire 2 is a stub under my fingers — and the bomb has shifted stages: the light turned blue, and the remaining wires re-colored to green, white, blue, red at positions 1, 3, 4, 5. Deaf announced all this aloud, so Mute has the new state too and is looking up stage two now. My tactile cross-check adds one thing Deaf's eyes cannot: confirmation that touch agrees with sight — four intact wires, no new parts, nothing else changed under my fingers. I'll pass that to Mute, ask that the same double-checked protocol be used for this stage (five-slot thumbs pattern, Deaf decodes aloud, Mute confirms, then and only then Deaf speaks go), and sign my standby to both. No hands on wires until Deaf's voice says so.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here — first cut confirmed by touch: wire 2 is severed, and my fingers agree with Deaf's report. Current state as I feel it: four intact wires at positions 1, 3, 4, 5, cut stub at 2, no new parts anywhere on the bomb. Deaf sees the new colors — 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red, light now blue, display still 0 — so between my touch and their eyes you have the full stage-two state. Please look up this stage and use the same safe protocol as before: gesture Deaf the five-slot pattern, thumbs up on the wire to cut and thumbs down on the rest, in position order; Deaf speaks the decode aloud; then you confirm with thumbs up or correct the number; only after that does Deaf speak me the go. If the manual says this stage needs anything besides one wire cut — the display, the light, a sequence, a time limit — spell that out to Deaf in gestures too, since I can only act by Deaf's spoken word.")
gesture(symbols=["👍", "🤝", "🖐", "🤚", "👌"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, Mute's instruction is in and it matches our proven code: the wire pattern and the number both point to wire 1, the green one, and Mute signed go directly. The word is GO. Cut exactly wire 1, the green wire. One cut, only that wire, touch nothing else.

Deaf relays Mute's stage-two instruction, and this time the redundancy is built into a single message: the five-slot thumbs pattern and the number sign are two independent encodings, and Deaf confirms both point to wire 1, the green one — plus Mute bundled the go signal directly. Two encodings agreeing is the same safety as our two-round confirmation; the protocol holds, and the trigger discipline holds — Deaf's spoken word says GO, cut exactly wire 1, the green one, one cut, nothing else. My fingers are already on position 1. Executing.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
